nominal_error_budget.interpretation: design_budget_only; the scaled alpha deliberately exceeds it and drift remains

selection_basis.rule: burden-reduction-v1 (+ amendment 1) rules 1-4 on two development runs, then rule 5 blind on pulse-stable-confirm; adoption changes the stable policy only after one more live run (this policy's run)
selection_basis.lever: L5 replica (peer) discount, 30 s: a window whose 4-window context has no syscall ID that the other replicas of its workload did not show within 30 s carries no evidence; joint p, k2of2 at alpha x5
selection_basis.calibration: the refreshed calibration of pulse-next-run-model (unchanged since pulse-stable-confirm)

blind_result.run: pulse-stable-confirm (rates 6, 12, 24 per second, 964 replica-hours of normal)

selection_basis.live_implementation: detector/novelty.py (Signals, the offline definition) + pipeline/peer_exchange.py: each worker decides its own windows; the peers' window masks arrive over TCP (~20 ms), so the newest peer bucket can be incomplete at decision time; a lost peer means less discount, never less detection
known_gaps: p95 2.68-2.98 s: the <= 3 s tier with little margin; the < 2 s tier is not met
an attack running on every replica at once is discounted (the campaign attacks one replica)
benign new-process launches are still flagged at 84-89 %; the discount removes only behaviour the other replicas share
burden ~1.7 episodes/replica-hour is still ~17x the 0.1/h budget
workloads with one replica (or replicas without a peer window in 30 s) are never discounted

output_mode: shadow_preview_only; never emits alert or enforcement
evaluation_requirements: fresh normal soak plus fresh attack campaign with benign-exec controls; fast scoring; report idle and benign controls separately; do not tune after outcomes; the worker config must carry peer_exchange (planner adds it)
